channel.description: Recent content in Posts on Savvyness - Blog

item.title: Tik-Tok's US Asset Sale
item.description: In its efforts to avoid a ban within the US and its respective countries worldwide, TikTok and its parent company, ByteDance, have entered into a deal to sell off 80.1% of its US operations. A binding agreement has been reached with a group of investors comprising Oracle, Silver Lake, and MGX, who will take a 15% stake in a brand-new company called TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC. It will also retain a minority shareholding of 19.9%, but be controlled by a majority-American board of directors.

item.title: Chile's Right Wing Shift
item.description:
Jose Antonio Kast was elected as president in an decisive runoff against center-left candidate Jeannete Jara. Kast, leader of a Republican Party secured around 58% of the vote compared to Jara’s 42%. This victory marks a significant shift in perspective and ideological shift in Chile.

They have brought one of the most conservative government to power since it’s return to Democracy. Kast’s campaign was a platform of strict immigration rules and a better crackdown on crime. He is scheduledto replace President Boric and take the post from March 11.

item.title: Bondi Beach Terror Attack
item.description: On Sunday, December 14, two shooters-identified as 50-year-old Sajid Akram and his 24-year-old son Naveed-opened fire during a Hanukkah celebration at Archer Park in Bondi Beach, Sydney. Motivated by extremist ideologies, 16 people including one perpetrator, died, and 42 others were injured. Victims ages ranged from 10 to 87 years old. Australian authorities found two improvised explosive devices at the scene and detonated them. In response, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced a massive national gun buyback program on December 19-the largest since the 1996 Port Arthur massacre-to tighten firearm regulations across the country.

item.title: Southern Transitional Council
item.description: Something big happened in the southern part of Yemen on the 8th of December, 2025. A separatist movement that seeks a further degree of independence (and possibly separation) of the southern part of Yemen from the rest of it, known as the Southern Transitional Council, made a major military move to seize more territories in Yemen by lunching the Hadhramaut military offensive. In this attack, they were able to take custody of oil-rich territories and asserted control over all eight southern provinces. This marked the biggest development in Yemen since the civil conflict erupted more than a decade ago. This situation genuinely sparked fears that the south would soon declare itself an independent state, as it used to be before its unification with Yemen in 1990. At the same time, Saudi Arabia withdrew all of its troops from Aden, which is the chief city in the south of Yemen, home to the internationally recognized government. This appeared to be a significant step backwards for Saudi support. Intense fighting ensued between them, such that the airspace of Yemen was briefly closed, interfering with aerial movements. Overall, this has further complicated and divided Yemen’s already-splintered civil conflict. Experts have been explaining how this can be un-stable and make negotiations even more difficult.

item.title: Hong Kong Holds Legislative Council Elections
item.description: The Legislative Council election took place on December 7, 2025. The second such election was conducted after Beijing hauled Hong Kong’s electoral landscape in 2021 and only allowed “patriots” loyal to China to take part. The hopefuls were all vetted for the election, and no pro-democracy candidates participated after many were barred, jailed, or chose to boycott. Supporters claimed it ensured stability even in the aftermath of the 2019 protests. Others saw it as undemocratic since there was no competition and the results were biased to favor the Beijing camps. Meanwhile, voter turnout was low, at only 31.9% – a slight increase from 30.2% in 2021 but still near-record low participation levels – due to public discontent over a deadly fire the day before, which claimed more than 150 lives. All of the 90 seats were taken by pro-establishment lawmakers, reflecting ongoing tensions between security measures taken by Beijing and democratic freedoms.

item.title: Coup Attempt Failed in Benin
item.description:
Elements of Beninese Armed Force announced a coup attempt against President Patrice Talon. To do this, they seized the state television in the capital, Cotonou. It was led by Lieutenant Colonel Pascal Tigri who declared the formation of a military junta. The coup quickly failed due to strong responses and the Nigerian AirForce carried out airstrikes against the coup forces.

Regional bloc ECOWAS also announced deployment of troops from multiple West African countries. African countries are often thought to be poor. However, they are slowly gaining their pace and catching up. This also shows how eager African countries are to help each others in time of desperate needs as well.

item.title: Netflix to Buy Warner Bros
item.description:
Netflix announced that would buy Warner Bros for US $72 Billion. Discovery, who is making one of the largest mergers in entertainment history. This move reflects how streaming service are reshaping the global media industry.

By acquiring Warner Bros, Netflix could gain control over major film studio, television networks, and other franchise belonging to Warner Bros. Some argue that this would lead to more efficient production and a stronger competition to traditional media channels. There is also worries that the competition might end up getting reduced, and more people will lose jobs. This deal highlights how economically powerful streaming services are nowadays in this modern era.

item.title: Protest in Bulgaria Force Government Budget Withdrawal
item.description:
Tens of thousands of people from Bulgaria have taken part in protests against the corruption and the unbalanced budget plan. This protest happened in between December-2 and 4,2025. Protesters were especially mad about increase in tax and the government was accused of mismanaging public funds while normal citizens struggled even for basic necessicity.

As the protesters spread to major cities, more pressure was put on Prime Minister Rosen. The Bulgarian Parliament withdrew the draft budget in response and was able to ease immediate tensions. However, some still continue to call for resignation of the officials. This event showed the effect of Public Pressure and how it can influence governments decision.

item.title: Cyclone Hits Indonesia and Sri-Lanka
item.description:
Severe weather in Indian Ocean region has been causing major humanitarian disasters. Cyclone Senyar is leading to catastrophic flooding in Indonesia. Sri-Lanka is also suffering a similar fate due to Cyclone Ditwah. The total death toll over both of them amount to over 900.

These disasters are overwhelming local emergency services as well so even getting help can become quite hard. Especially in local and remote areas, extreme weather and extreme condition can make it almost for emergency services to reach to. This is greatly increasing the risk of large scale loss among these countries.

item.title: Brazil Jails Jair Bolsonaro as Coup Plot Sentence Starts
item.description: On November 25th, former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro received a 27-year sentencing to a correctional facility following a conviction for orchestrating a plot to topple Brazil’s transition to a democracy after the 2022 election. The verdict marked the culmination of one of the most important cases of accountability in modern Brazilian history. The conviction of Bolsonaro and his associates proved that they had been planning to corrupt Brazilian institutions of democracy and had engaged in the planning of violent actions aimed at elected leaders. The action was perceived by both critics and supporters of Bolsonaro as a bold stand on defending democracy while others perceived it as political persecution.

item.title: Russian Missile Strikes Ukrainian Cities
item.description:
Russian missile and drone attacks have killed dozens of citizens including atleast 31 people in a ballistic missile strike on a residential apartment in Ternopil. The attack single-handedly created more than 100injured, and, many remained missing under rubble as rescue teams continue their search.

The strikes were one of the deadliest of the year and targeted densely populated areas. Ukrainian officials have deemed the attacks as war crimes. International reactions are renewing calls for stronger air defence support. The incident is highlighting the ongoing effect of the war on innocent civilians ; even those far from the front line.

item.title: Famine Deepens as Aid Groups Withdraw
item.description:
Medecins Sans Frontieres withdrew staffs from a hospital located in central Darfur after repeated attacks on November 25. The attacks also included the killing of a stretcher bearer. This decision has come through after famine was officially declared in parts of Sudan.

This is highlighting the collapse of humanitarian access amid fighting between the Sudanese Armed Force and the Rapid Support Forces. Aid agencies have warned that civilians were being trapped without foods and protection. MSF also stated that it would not return safety for the people is guaranteed.

item.title: Saudi Named Major Non NATO Ally
item.description:
Saudi Arabia, a major non-NATO ally, as declared by President Trump on November 18. They have signed a deal that enables them to freely trade military weapons including F-35 Fighter jets. The announcement is based on civil nuclear cooperation between Saudi and USA.

This move has signaled a significant strengthening of both nations. It also signs toward a bilateral ties and a shift in the US Middle East strategy. Supporters argue it is for enhancing security, critics are raising questions about human rights and arms proliferation. This grants Saudi and US preferential access to both countries resources and defence cooperation.

item.title: Gaza Peace Plan
item.description:
The United Nations Security Council recently approved a US-drafted peace plan resolution for Gaza. The resolution backed the creation of an International Stabilization Force in case something breaks out again. It’s main task would be to oversee post-conflict governance and security.

This marked a rare consensus at the Security Council on Gaza after many months of unsuccessful attempts. While people and critics are questioning the enforcement, troop contributions and other things, the vote reflected mounting an International pressure to move beyond just ordinary ceasefire and more toward a longer term success.

item.title: Ceasefire Violations and Ongoing Hostage Body Returns in Gaza
item.description:
The Gaza ceasefire is continuosly facing serious tests in mid November. Hamas has returned the remains of several Israeli hostages, however, they are still delaying fully returning all the body and are accusing Israel of violations. Israel has reported attacks near demarcation lines that killed soldiers and responded with air-strikes.

Both sides are accusing of/are breaching the deal. The US has warned them off resuming operations if Hamas did not fully comply. The exchanges underscored greatly and the deal’s fragility despite initial progress.

item.title: Rh null : The rarest blood type
item.description:
Approximately only one in six million people have the blood type : Rh Null.

Blood transfusion have changed the way modern treatments work. Anyone who is ever injured and in need of blood can just simply get it by transfusing it. You may think everyone is benefited from this. However, you could not be more wrong.

There are lots of people with rare blood types. In this, there are currently 50 known people who are not able to take benefit of this at all. This is because they have the blood type Rh Null. This specific blood type is so rare to find that blood transfusion is just out of the way. This specific blood is so rare that getting a transfusion is almost impossible. People with this blood type are actually encouraged to freeze their own blood for long term use in case something were too happen. This blood type also has another name due to its rarity, it’s often referred to as the ‘Golden Blood’.

item.title: Deadliest Police Operation Rio De Janeiro
item.description: The police in Brazil initiated an anti-crime crackdown, dubbed Operation Containment, against the strongholds of Comando Vermelho in Rio de Janeiro, resulting in a record number of at least 132 fatalities, including four police officers, and 81 arrests by November 10, 2025. This is the deadliest single police operation staged in the city. While the government lauded it as a landmark crackdown against crime syndicates, human rights activists deplored the overuse of force by the police, resulting in the loss of civilian lives.

item.title: Major Suicide Bombing in Islamabad
item.description: A suicide bombing outside a court in Islamabad killed 12 and injured more than 20 people. Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi accused Afgan nationals to plan and carry out the attack. The tensions between the countries has escalated in the 2025 Afghanistan-Pakistan conflict. Pakistan is accusing the Taliban of sheltering militants. The attack underscored ongoing security challenges in Pakistan and further made situations more complicated about the cross-broder relations.

item.title: Typhoon Kalmaegi Devastates Philippines
item.description:
Coastal Countries are getting hit by typhoons more and more frequently. This subtle change is due to climate change caused by human actions. Typhoon Kalmaegi caused catastrophic damage across Visayas and Mindanao. The total death confirmed till now is around 142. Over 127 are missing.

Floods, landslides and other disasters are following this typhoon. Philippine president Bongbong Marcos declared a national state of calamity to mobilize emergency resources. This ranks among the deadliest typhoons to ever hit Philippines.

item.title: Capture of El Fasher and Al Fashir
item.description: IPC officially confirmed famine in Darfur and South Kordofan on 3rd of November,2025. Sudan’s humanitarian crisis further escalated to devastating heights as international monitors announced that famine had officially struck parts of Sudan, including the regions of Darfur and South Kordofan. This announcement came at such a time when escalation of hostilities between Sudanese Armed Forces and RSF continued to prevent aid from being taken to those in need, including those without access to food, medicine, or shelter. At practically the same time, RSF forces staged yet another deadliest attack of the war thus far, targeting civilians in North Kordofan, including their shelter and funeral processions, resulting in dozens of deaths, although other sources indicate that the fatalities from these encounters may not be so low. This attack came on the heels of RSF forces capturing El Fasher, yet another major city in the region of Darfur, creating further mayhem in that region. These events underscored the direct role that the war is playing in bringing harm to Sudan’s civilians and underscored the need for unhindered humanitarian access into Sudan.

item.title: Major US Off Year Election
item.description:
The results for the off-year elections are out and the results are quite remarkable.

Avigali Spanberger (Democrat) was elected the governor of Virginia and became the first female governor for a state.

Zohran Mamdani was elected the Mayor of NYC, becoming the first ever Muslim and South-American mayor of a state.

On it’s own, it might sound like small achievements , however, these wins can be seen as democratic moments. Such momentum should be carried forward and achieve diversity in Leadership. This applies especially to countries where male are still quite seen to be more competent and dominant. While this may not be the case in USA, it’s still there for the case of Politics.

item.title: Impeachment and Removal of Peruvian President
item.description: As if its tradition of political tumult needed further validation, Peru’s cycle of election, impeachment, and scandal reached a climactic turn of events with President Dina Boluarte being voted out of office on October 10, 2025, by a shocking 124-0 tally. What else could have triggered this shocking moment of collective political angst if not the government’s inept handling of a raging crime wave? When President Boluarte failed to turn up for a mandated impeachment hearing at Congress, the result was unprecedented unanimity.

item.title: Sanae Takachi's Historic Rise
item.description:
A moment that will be studied for generations, Takaichi shattered one of the hardest ceilings ceilings global politics on October-10,2025.After a tense liberal democratic party emerged victorious, Takaichi earned the title of Japan’s first female Prime Minister. Her election marks a shift in cultural view of politics being a male job in a country like Japan.

She, known for her conservative views and advanced economical politics won the election on her formidable reputation and policy. She is someone who has achieved something revolutionary. Supporters see her as the “Iron-Lady” that Japan needs to navigate to a more stagnant domestic economy.

item.title: Historic Nobel Peace Prize Awarded to Maria Corina
item.description: On October 10, 2025, the Norwegian Nobel Committee notified the world of its intention by declaring María Corina Machado a Nobel Peace Prize winner. The Norwegian Nobel Committee stated that Machado won “for her tireless, non-violent struggle for the restoration of democracy in Venezuela.” A woman who has faced physical injury, bans from international travel, and political disqualification. To many, it means more than simply an individual’s honor; it can symbolize millions of Venezuelans who have struggled to be heard.

item.title: Hurricane Melissa Reaches Category 5
item.description: Hurricane Melissa strengthened into a Category 5 hurricane with winds of 185 mph and struck in southwest Jamaica on Sunday, October 7, 2025. The hurricane caused widespread destruction, power outages, and evacuations in the island nation, including reports of fatalities and flooding. A national emergency has been declared in Jamaica, and aid is being sent to the island nation as the hurricane threatens other Caribbean countries and the Gulf coast of the United States.

item.title: Phase 1 of Gaza Ceasefire
item.description: October 3, 2025, Hamas agreed to parts of U.S. President Donald Trump’s 20-point Gaza ceasefire plan, including hostage releases and administrative handover. By Tuesday, October 7, the Israeli cabinet approved the deal, and the ceasefire took effect with IDF withdrawal to agreed lines. Hamas began returning bodies of deceased hostages, while Israel released over 1,900 Palestinian detainees. The agreement marked the first major de-escalation in the conflict in nearly two years, though both sides accused each other of early violations.

item.title: Chernobyl Power Outage After Russian Drone Strike
item.description: The “emergency situation” at the Ukrainian-held nuclear plant near Kiev was announced by the Ukrainian Ministry of Energy on Wednesday, October 1, 2025. The declaration was a result of a Russian drone strike at the Ukrainian-held Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant, resulting in a three-hour power outage at the New Safe Confinement structure designed to contain radioactive materials from the 1986 nuclear disaster. The cause of the outage resulted from the destruction of a nearby energy facility in Slavutych. The generators were activated, and a state of panic ensued.

item.title: Trump Administration Deploys National Guards to Cities Citing Crime
item.description:
On Monday, September 15th , September, American President Trump ordered it’s army to cities such as Tennessee and Memphis to supposedly combat crime. Along with this, he extended the deployment areas to Portland and Oregon describing those cities as war destroyed.

These actions marked a significant federal intervention in local law enforcement and raising of legal and constitutional debates over his decisions. Questions about state sovereign, local law enforcement, and militarizing of policing were also raised. The use of military forces on it’s own soil during peacetime does not fit the situation, said some Citizens.

item.title: Cebu Earthquake in Philippines
item.description:
Magnitude 6.9 Cebu struck Philippines on Thursday, September 25,2025 causing widespread structural damage, power outage, and at least 60 confirmed death. Thousands of civilians were affected and had to possibly relocate temporarily.

The rescue operation continued for days after the incident. It highlighted Philippines weakness to seismic movements and had national emergency declarations and international support on site.

item.title: UN Security Reimposes Sanctions on Iran
item.description:
September-24,2025, UN Security Council voted to reinstate economic and military sanctions on Iran under the snapback mechanism of Resolution 2231 after several members of EU triggered it. The countries to trigger it include :- France, Germany, United Kingdom, and some other. This was done as Iran’s nuclear escalation was non-cooperative with the IAEA, and failure to comply with JCPOA obligations.

This imposition is going to mark a major escalation in Iran’s nuclear crisis and affect it’s exports. Banking access, arms trade, and others are also affected. It might also prompt strong condemnation from Tehran and it’s other allies.

item.title: Palestine Recognised by Multiple Nations
item.description: On Sunday, the 21st of September, 2025, Australia, Canada, Portugal, and the United Kingdom officially recognized Palestine as a sovereign state. Canada became the first member of the G7 to make the move. This action can also be seen as a culmination of months of diplomatic pressure, which is greatly attributed to the Gaza crisis, famine declaration, and UN reports. This move greatly solidified the status of Palestine as a sovereign state while further distancing Israel from the rest of the world.

item.title: Historic Diplomatic Moves and Prisoner Releases in Belarus
item.description:
52 political prisoners, including 14 foreign nationals were released from Belarus on September-11,2025. This was done with negotiations with the US. In response to releasing them, the US replied by lifting the sanctions on Belarusian flagcarrier Belavia.

This rare occasion amid going repression came and signaled a thaw in Belarus-US relations. By Monday, September-15,2025, Mikola Statkevich was returned to penal colony after refusing deportation to Lithuania.

item.title: Emmy Awards 2025
item.description:
####The Studio#### was the most-nominated first year comedy series with 23 nominations. The 77th Emmy Awards held on Sunday, September-14, 2025 produced quite a few groundbreaking decisions and moments. The Studio took home the Outstanding Comedy Series award. The Pitts took home the Outstanding Drama Series while Anthology Series went to Adolescence.

For the first time ever in the history of Emmy awards, every nominee had atleast one woman on writing team for the category of Outstanding Writing for a Comedy Series. Owen Cooper became the youngest male Emmy winner ever. The ceremony for the Emmy-2025 was widely praised for it’s diversity and recognition of talent.

item.title: Massive Escalation and Chaos in Nepal's Gen-Z Protest
item.description: On September-8,2025, anti-government protests in Kathmandu and major cities of Nepal turned deadly when police opened fire. Normally, this was supposed to be a peace protest and there was supposed to be no gun shots. However, Gen-Z anger over corruption and the protest not coming to a halt, the police opened fire, first with rubber bullets, then with real bullets. This enraged the public even more and the protest ultimately erupted with rage and did not back down until Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli resigned.

item.title: Russian Drone Incursion Into Poland
item.description:
Russian drone 250 km into Polish airspace during large-scale attack on Ukraine. On Wednesday, September 10, 2025, 19 Russian drone strayed from their original attack path to Ukraine and entered Polish airspace. The Polish airforce along with NATO allies shot down four drones. This was the first direct engagement of Russian equipment to other country than Ukraine since war began.

The incident created quite a tension between NATO and Russia. This also raised fears of an even wider miscalculation and accident breakout of drones in other areas. To counter this, a three month flight ban was kept over Polish airspsace.

item.title: Belgium's Conditional Recognition of Palestine
item.description: In early September of 2025, Belgium gave a clear indication that conflict between Israel and Palestine would change significantly. In announcement of this new direction, the Belgian foreign minister stated that Belgium would recognize Palestine as a state at the United Nations, but only if conditions were met. These conditions would mean that there would be permission for hostages being held in Gaza to be set free, alongside Hamas being removed from power in Gaza.

item.title: Surge in Sales of Electronics
item.description:
S.K.’s ( South Korea ) trade ministry said that semi-conductor reached all time high sales. The total sales was approximately around $15 Billion.
This marked a nearly one-third increase year by year which contributed to monthly exports reaching up to $50 Billion dollars. This significantly highlights the strength of S.K. when it comes to making chip/chipsets.

The likely cause of such an immense increase in sales is likely due to AI-related business needing high end systems. The tariffs was immense on the products, however Korea’s strength in technology caused it to not be affected at all. The tariffs likely made the people not trust shady sellers and to rather directly get them from a trusted source which was Samsung of Korea. This enabled them to not be affected even though tariffs were increasing.

item.title: Massive Earthquake Hits Afghanistan
item.description:
An earthquake of a magnitude around 6.0 struck near Jalalbad in Nangarhar province in eastern Afghanistan. Official reports confirm around 610 deaths and over 1300 injured. This causes it to be one of the most deadly earthquakes in the country in recent history.

The victims were trapped by the debris of their homes and buildings in rural areas. The disaster added to the list of challenges facing Afghanistan, including food shortages and limited access to aid. Rescue work took several days, and aid groups from around the world offered to assist. Despite so much efforts, victims are still in a state of suffering.

item.title: Political Upheavel and Protest - Indonesia
item.description:
The protest in Jakartha, Indonesia which was led by students and labour unions has Escalated. The protest is going viral all over the internet for the use of flags of “One-Piece”. The flag is meant to symbolise freedom as in the freedom the pirates have in One-Piece. After the death of 21 year old taxi driver Affan Kurniawan, the protest took off in over 30 provinces.

The mobs turned violent after the death and looting homes of parliament members and ministers became common. The One-Piece flag was one of the main symbol they used to go against the government. President Prabowo Subianto responded to this by revoking allowances and imposing foreign travel restrictions. The protest reflected deep frustration over governance and economic issue.

item.title: Record Breaking Famine Declaration in Gaza
item.description:
The IPC ( Integrated Food Security Phase Classification ), on Friday, August 22 officially declared famine (search what it means) in Gaza Governorate with condition in the North equally or even worse. The Israeli side disputed the findings. If condition don’t change, it could spread to Deir al-Balah and Khan Younis by end of September.

This marked the first famine declaration in a conflict zone in a long time. This triggered urgent calls for unrestricted humantarian corridors. Starvation related to deaths are rising and showing an already catasthropic humanitarian situation. Child malnutrition rates reached record-breaking high levels and starvation death rates also skyrocketed.

item.title: Air Canada Flight Attendants Strike Resolution
item.description: The Air Canada crew, represented by the Canadian Union of Public Employees, went on strike yet again. Despite a government-imposed arbitration requirement to settle the employees down, the strike grounded all flights. Over 700 flights per day were delayed or grounded. This impacted 130,000 passengers daily. The airline had put a halt to resumption of flights again because of the strike. A tentative agreement was obtained on Tuesday, August 19, 2025, allowing flights to resume gradually. The strike between the airline crew and the employees is a reflection of the widening gap between the administration and employees regarding the contracts and claims. Travelers were disrupted because of the strike.

item.title: Flood across Pakistan
item.description:
Heavy monsoon rains have triggered immense flooding in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province in Pakistan starting around August 14. The total death is rising day by day and is currently at around 321 deaths. This severe flooding has caused entire villages to be submerged, thousands to be displaced and heavy damage to infrastructure.

On August 15, a government helicopter despached for flood relief was also crashed due to bad and unstable weather. The flood has displaced more than 100k civilians. International support for the area has been urged as urgent support. The scale of destruction is quite large and is questioning climate resilience and how pakistan prepares for such scenarios.

item.title: Trump Putin Summit in Alaska on Ukraine Peace
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump announces a summit meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin to be held on Friday, August 15, 2025, at a venue to be located in Alaska, USA. The aim of the meeting is to find a way to bring an end to the Russian invasion of Ukraine on a date no later than Sunday, August 10, 2025. The meeting between Trump and Putin took place sans Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who was not invited to the meeting, a development that drew criticism from Ukraine and some of its European allies, who have expressed concerns over the chances of concessions by Russia on Ukraine territory. The meeting between Trump and Putin comes at a time when Russia is launching some of the biggest attacks on Ukraine territory using ground attacks, such as the one launched on August 11, 2025, to capture Dobropillia, a town located in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine. The meeting is also at a time when Ukraine is launching drone attacks on Russia territory. The meeting between Trump and Putin is a significant development in the Ukraine-Russia conflict, given Trump’s resolve to find a way to bring an end to the conflict, which has been ongoing for a while.

item.title: Diplomatic Breakthrough between US and Russia
item.description:
President Donand Trump Ordered two U.S. Navy nuclear submarines to be repositioned near Russia. This was done according to Trump in response to “provocative statements” by previous Russian President Dmitry Medvedev. This escalated verbral tensions in the moddle of ongoing Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian infrastructure.

By August-8, a major diplomatic achievement was achieved when Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and Illham Aliyev of Ajerbaijan met Trump at the White House to sign a peace agreement ending decades of conflict. This also included commitments to non-aggression and development in the Zangezur corridor faciliated by U.S. . This was a Trump-brokered success contrasting U.S.-Russia nuclear signaling.

item.title: Trump implements Tariffs under related trade actions
item.description:
Friday, August-1st, President Trump applied his Broader Trade Policy. This policy brought upon many countries “tariffs”. U.S. tariffs swept imports fromover 90 countries after a 90 day preparation pause, including 35% on some Canadian goods and 50% on Brazilian goods, with a baseline of around 30% varying by country or balance.

By today, additional escalations included increase on Indian imports to around 50% and the tariffs aimed at addressing trade deficits. This was meant for a greater good as said by Trump, however the world has replied to this with economic concerns with potential retaliation and higher consumption costs. Reports highlighted Canada’s significant hit and negotiations for some countries. Trump does not seem to want to back away from this claim of his.

item.title: Cambodia-Thailand border clashes escales
item.description: Armed clashes erupted near Prasat Ta Muen Thom temple along Cambodia-Thailand border. This incident on Thursday, July-24,2025 caused thousands of displacement among civilians. According to reports, at least 14 people were killed and 46 injured on the Thai side with additional casualties on both sides. The cause for this incident was long standing tention between the two nations about border territory. Thailand later on declared martial law in border districts, highlighting regional tensions and the need for diploatic intervention to prevent wide escalation of the incident.

item.title: Deadly Air Force crash in Dhaka
item.description: Bangladesh Air Force FT-7BG! ( Chengdu 7-J variant ) training aircraft crashed shortly after takeoff from base. It plunged into the Milestone School and College in Uttara,Dhaka. This incident lead to around 31 death and over 50 injured. Some reports even cite upto 27 death among civilians and students. This crash caused widespread destruction on the educational site drawing the attention of nation which lead to a nation wide mourning. The investigation on the crash till now are not clear yet. However, it’s believed to be mechanical orpilot error. It ranks as one of the most deadly accident involving military planes in the recent history of Bangladesh.

item.title: NATO Allies To Buy Weapons from US
item.description: President Trump announced that NATO membered countries / allies ave agreed to purchase U.S. made weapons. This also includes Patriot air defence missile systems. It seems the main objective of U.S. is to sell weapons to Ukraine during this War period to profit for itself. Trump described the deal as a major step forward, emphasizing that European nations would finance the purchases directly, with weapons drawn from U.S. stockpiles and replenished by American production. He highlighted that the Patriot systems are critical for Ukrain’s air defence against Russia.

item.title: Somali Civil War, Recapture of village Tardo
item.description: A village in Hiiraan region of Hirshabelle state, central Somalia called Tardo VIllage was under Somali National Army Force. This was recaptured by Al-Shabaab militants on July-13/14. The village had been held by a small Somali Army force. Reports indicate that this takeover happened with very-little resistance after government-aligned forces withdrew. This formed part was a part of strategic triangle control to dustrupt supply lines, encirclepositions, and displace thousands. The advance highlighted setbacks for Somali conunter measure efforts amid political divisions.

item.title: Gaza War - Israel strikes on water collection point
item.description: July 13,2025 , on a Sunday, an Israeli airstrike hit a water distribution point in Nuseirat refugee camp, central Gaza Strip. Palestinian health officials at AI-Awda hospitals reported the death of 10 people minimum. This included six childrens as well. Many wounded civilians queued for water due to severe shortage caused by this incident. The overall death in Gaza has reached well over 58,000 after this long period of conflict.

item.title: Earths 3rd Warmest Record
item.description: NOAA’s (National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration ) climate report confirms that July 2025 as the third warmest July globally on record. This contributes to 2025 being one of the warmest year ever recorded. The month started off warm and wet and is going on the same. Countries like US also experienced floods and all. These trends align with ongoing global warming and climate change. This data also contributes greatly to studying climate change. This is likely caused due to Human actions such as pollution, emmision of gases lack of effort to minimise it. This asks for international effort to reduce emmissions and pollution globally.

item.title: Global Trade Booming despite the Tariffs
item.description: Global trade expanded by an estimated $300 billion in the first half of 2025, growing at an estimated 1.5% in the first quarter and projections showing 2% growth in the second. Although President Trump is busy dumping Tariff’s and causing massive geo-political issues among itself and other countries, global Trades are going off at a steady pace.

item.title: BTS Reunion
item.description:
K-pop boy-band group BTS officially announces it’s reunion and a reunion tour around the world. Such an act has caused massive hype among it’s fans in the K-pop industry. Not just among fans, it has also succeeded to take over other industry. One of it’s most significant effect is in the stock for HYBE Co. and it also crashed major ticketing server globally.

item.title: Comet 3I-ATLAS Discovered as Potentially Oldest Object
item.description:
A telescope funded by NASA , The Asteroid Terrestrial-Impact Last Alert System, discovers Comet 3I/ATLAS. This intestellar object is believed to possibly be the oldest known comet till date. This is valuable data on Intestellar and brings us one step closer to the start of time and space itself.

This data can help know more about the “Big-Bang” which is believed to be the origin of the entire universe itself. It can help us inch ever so closer to understanding how it all started. It can also possibly help find new particles left to be undiscovered till yet that were formed close to the Big Bang itself.

item.title: USAID Shuttered
item.description:
On July-1st, 2025, President Donald Trump officially ended it’s agency for International Department. This had a huge effect on not just the U.S. but also other countries. It single handedly ended 64 years (approx.) of centralized American aid to 100+ countries. This had a huge effect on a lot of countries receiving aid and help from the US.

Thid had more effect in some parts of the world such as Asia and Africa. It has caused immediate cut-off of health, education and infrastructure support on them. This not only signifies the loss of foreign aid from U.S.A. but also how it might handle foreign related things later on. It has moved away from a typical “soft power” to more of a transaction based power rule by the Government.

item.title: Largest Health Care Fraud Taken Down
item.description: The justice Department in US announced it’s results of 2025 National Health care Fraud takedown which caused criminal charges against around 300 defendants. The defendants include 96 Doctors, nurse practioner, pharmacists and other liscened medical practioners. This happened in 50 federal districts and exposed schemes involving over $14 Billion in intended loss. The takedown involved federal and state law enforcement across multiple agency in the country. This is the largest fraud ever done in US medical history with over $13 Billion in fraud money. It caused millions of dollars worth of property to be seized by the government. This operation prevented billions from being paid out through proactive data analysis by DOJ’s Health Care Fraud Unit.
